scope: Public publisher and institutional records searched at BBC, British Pathé, BFI/IWM, Indiana University, Smithsonian, National Library of Jamaica, UWI and jazz session publishers. This is a bounded online search, not an exhaustive inventory of uncatalogued or offline archives.

recordings.performer_connection: Kingston-born Dan Kildare; issued as Joan Sawyer’s Persian Garden Orchestra
recordings.evidence: Collector’s original-recording page identifies specific track/date/matrix. Reissue publisher independently identifies Kingston birth and 1914 recordings. Publisher volume two dates recording debut 5 May; that is not substituted for the collector’s 6 May track date.
recordings.access: Listen on collector’s page; audio not copied or embedded because source prohibits reposting/commercial use. Publisher volumes provide further catalog/purchase routes.

recordings.jamaican_voice: Unnamed Jamaican nurse, as identified by CD41 original release notes

recordings.kind: Edited reporter/passenger exchanges in a newsreel
recordings.evidence: Official YouTube oEmbed retrieved HTTP 200 and identifies British Pathé/title. Issue/release date corroborated by film researcher Luke McKernan's account.
recordings.speaker_origin_limit: Newsreel labels do not authenticate individual birthplaces of unnamed speakers. Lord Kitchener's singing is Trinidadian performance, not a Jamaican natural-speech sample.

recordings.kind: Stage-managed wartime broadcast film; comparison material
recordings.evidence: Official YouTube oEmbed retrieved HTTP 200 identifying BFI/title. BFI description explicitly identifies staged messages; IWM CCE 211 explains the distinct shorter cut.
Publisher session notes identify Spike Hughes Orchestra, Thompson, Decca F.2323-A and date/place. Alpha's separate example is dated 23 January 1931 and is not conflated with this session.

not_verified: A publicly playable natural-conversation recording from 1931 was not authenticated in this search; non-discovery is not evidence of nonexistence.
UWI oral histories concerning 1938 may be later recollections; subject date is not a recording date.
Indiana University's complete 1921 collection is catalogued as sung/spoken, but the selected public examples are performances. The full catalog's authorized-user access was not bypassed.
BBC, Spotify, Indiana University and YouTube player HTTP/metadata checks do not prove audible playback in the visitor's browser.
No pre-1921 natural-conversation recording or earlier recording made in Jamaica was authenticated in this bounded search. Kildare’s recordings are overseas performances, not proof of either claim.
